questions.prompt: A Docker build compiles in an SDK stage and copies only output into a fresh runtime stage. What can remain outside the final image?

choices.text: The final stage’s selected base image.
Every file required by the application process.
The SDK and unused build artifacts.
All runtime files copied by COPY --from.

questions.explanation: A separate final stage includes its base and selected artifacts. It need not include the SDK or unused build output.

sources.title: Docker multi-stage builds
sources.claim: Each FROM starts a build stage and COPY --from selectively copies artifacts without including all earlier-stage tools.

questions.prompt: Every source edit reruns dependency installation because COPY . . precedes it. Which ordering improves cache reuse?

choices.text: Disable the build cache for every development build.
Copy dependency manifests, install, then copy changing source.
Copy all source first and add another identical install step.
Delete dependency manifests so installs cannot detect changes.

questions.explanation: Stable dependency inputs should precede frequently changing source. Repeating installation or disabling cache does not preserve the reusable dependency layer.

sources.title: Optimize cache usage in builds
sources.claim: Put infrequently changing dependency inputs before frequently changing source files; changes invalidate their layer and subsequent dependent layers.

questions.prompt: A shell-form ENTRYPOINT launches the app under a shell, and stop signals do not reach it as expected. Which form addresses the wrapper?

choices.text: Use exec-form ENTRYPOINT for the application executable.
Add EXPOSE so Docker forwards process signals.
Retain the implicit shell wrapper and rely on EXPOSE for process cleanup.
Keep shell-form startup and assume CMD arguments remove its shell wrapper.

questions.explanation: Exec form avoids the implicit shell wrapper and supports direct signal delivery to the main process. EXPOSE and CMD arguments do not remove a shell-form ENTRYPOINT wrapper.

sources.title: Dockerfile reference
sources.claim: Exec-form ENTRYPOINT runs the executable without a shell wrapper; shell-form startup can prevent signals from reaching the application process.

questions.prompt: A private registry credential is passed through a Dockerfile ENV instruction. What is the safer build mechanism?

choices.text: Keep ENV and obscure the credential with Base64.
Commit the credential file so every build can reproduce it.
Delete the credential only in a later image layer.
Supply it through a BuildKit secret mount.

questions.explanation: Secret mounts expose build credentials temporarily. ENV, source commits and earlier persisted layers can disclose them; encoding is not protection.

sources.title: Docker build secrets
sources.claim: Docker build arguments and environment variables are unsuitable for build secrets; secret mounts expose values temporarily during build instructions.

questions.prompt: A build refers to its compilation stage by numeric index, which breaks after stage reordering. What improves maintainability?

choices.text: Use ordinary COPY without --from and assume it reads the earlier stage.
Rename a build argument and assume COPY --from treats it as a declared stage.
Name the stage and reference that name.
Use RUN cp and assume files from earlier stages share the current filesystem.

questions.explanation: AS assigns a stage name, and COPY --from can reference it. Earlier stages do not share the current stage filesystem; ordinary COPY reads the build context, and a build argument is not a stage declaration.

sources.title: Docker multi-stage builds
sources.claim: Named stages can be referenced through COPY --from and remain stable under reordering.

questions.prompt: A repository sends logs and local dependency folders as build context. Which change reduces unnecessary input?

choices.text: Install dependencies again after every source copy.
Exclude irrelevant files with .dockerignore.
Copy every log into the final image for cache reuse.
Move unwanted files to a later COPY instruction without excluding them from context.

questions.explanation: The ignore file removes unneeded context files. Extra copying and repeated installation add work rather than reducing input.

sources.title: Optimize cache usage in builds
sources.claim: A small build context and .dockerignore avoid unnecessary transferred inputs.

questions.prompt: Which multi-stage build statements hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A stage name refers to the same thing as a runtime environment variable.
Multi-stage builds require separate Dockerfiles for each stage.
Each FROM begins a new stage that may use a different base.
COPY --from can copy selected artifacts from another stage.
All earlier-stage tools automatically become final-image layers.

questions.explanation: A is incorrect: Stage names identify build stages. B is incorrect: One Dockerfile can define multiple stages. C is correct: Stages can separate building from running. D is correct: It does not copy the entire earlier image. E is incorrect: A fresh final stage can leave them behind.

sources.title: Docker multi-stage builds
sources.claim: Each FROM starts a build stage and COPY --from selectively copies artifacts without including all earlier-stage tools.

questions.prompt: Which choices improve Docker build cache use? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Copy all frequently changing files before dependency installation for best reuse.
Place expensive steps with stable inputs earlier in the build.
Keep the build context small with an appropriate .dockerignore.
Use cache mounts for reusable package-download data where appropriate.
Assume a changed earlier layer leaves all later dependent layers reusable.

questions.explanation: A is incorrect: This invalidates the dependency layer on source changes. B is correct: Later source edits need not invalidate those steps. C is correct: Unneeded files increase transfer and invalidation risk. D is correct: They preserve cache data across builds. E is incorrect: Subsequent dependent layers must rebuild.

sources.title: Optimize cache usage in builds
sources.claim: Put infrequently changing dependency inputs before frequently changing source files; changes invalidate their layer and subsequent dependent layers.

questions.prompt: Which startup statements follow Dockerfile semantics? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Exec-form ENTRYPOINT avoids the implicit command shell.
Shell-form ENTRYPOINT can interfere with signal delivery to its child.
Exec-form arguments always expand shell variables automatically.
EXPOSE controls whether the application receives termination signals.
Changing only COPY order changes shell-form startup into exec form.

questions.explanation: A is correct: The application can be the container’s main process. B is correct: The shell wrapper changes process relationships. C is incorrect: There is no shell to perform that expansion. D is incorrect: EXPOSE describes network ports, not process signals. E is incorrect: Startup syntax is controlled by ENTRYPOINT or CMD.

sources.title: Dockerfile reference
sources.claim: Exec-form ENTRYPOINT runs the executable without a shell wrapper; shell-form startup can prevent signals from reaching the application process.

questions.prompt: Which secret-handling choices follow Docker guidance? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A secret mount is available for the relevant build instruction.
Use SSH mounts for supported private Git access.
Use ENV as the recommended storage for private build credentials.
Treat Base64 in a build argument as encryption of the secret.
Pass the secret to the build and consume it through a secret mount.

questions.explanation: A is correct: Its access is temporary rather than an ordinary image file. B is correct: They expose SSH credentials or sockets during the build. C is incorrect: Environment values can persist in the image. D is incorrect: Encoding does not prevent disclosure. E is correct: Both client supply and Dockerfile consumption are needed.

sources.title: Docker build secrets
sources.claim: Docker build arguments and environment variables are unsuitable for build secrets; secret mounts expose values temporarily during build instructions.
